entries.title: United flight from Chicago diverted to Wisconsin due to 'unruly passenger'
entries.summary: <p>A United Airlines flight had to be diverted due to an "unruly passenger" shortly after leaving O'Hare International Airport on Friday night. </p><p>United Airlines flight 2005, traveling from O'Hare to Minneapolis-Saint Paul International Airport, landed safely at the Dane County Regional Airport in Madison, Wisconsin, around 9:10 p.m., the airline said in a statement. </p><p>The plane had to divert due to a "security concern with an unruly passenger," the airline said. </p><p>The FBI was notified of the incident and the FBI Milwaukee's Madison Resident Agency and local law enforcement responded at the tarmac. </p><p>The passenger was taken into custody by the Dane County Sheriff’s Office, according to the FBI. Afterwards the flight resumed and landed in Minneapolis around 2:19 a.m. Saturday. </p>

entries.title: Winner downs nearly 9 dogs while competing at Windy City Hot Dog Fest
entries.summary: <p>If you happened to walk by the intersection of North Milwaukee and West Belle Plaine avenues on Saturday afternoon, you may have heard a roaring, three-word chant.</p><p><i>Frank the Tank! Frank the Tank! Frank the Tank!</i></p><p>At least 1,000 people cheered on the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/food-drink/2025/05/31/winning-wiener-windy-city-hot-dog-fest-fans-will-vote-on-the-top-dog" >reigning champion</a> of the hot dog-eating contest at the annual <a class="Link" href="https://chicagoevents.com/event/windy-city-hot-dog-fest/" target="_blank" >Windy City Hot Dog Fest</a> in Portage Park. By the time the announcer yelled “dogs down” at the end of the five-minute competition, 'the Tank' — aka Frank Wach — had put away 8 1/2 wieners.</p><p>He beat out four other contestants and took home the hot dog trophy for a third year.</p><p>“I feel great,” said Wach, 72, of Norwood Park. “I do it for the fun of it and just to show that I’m not that old.”</p><p>When asked how he was feeling after eating six hot dogs, runner-up Greg Bartusiak said, “Not great.”</p><p>“This isn’t something anyone should strive for, really,” said Bartusiak, 35, of Portage Park, as he sipped a can of Coke. “It’s either the crowning point of all of my achievements in life or the low point of all of my achievements in life.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" entries.title: Bumpy trips end with White Sox for Jacob Gonzalez
entries.summary: <p>Like his travel Saturday, infielder <b>Jacob Gonzalez’s</b> trip to the big leagues hasn’t been straightforward.</p><p>On his 24th birthday, the former first-round pick was officially called up to the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" >White Sox</a>, taking the spot of the injured <b>Munetaka Murakami</b>. Before he could meet his new teammates, Gonzalez had to travel from Charlotte to Chicago, but his flight was delayed from 7:40 a.m. to 9:40 a.m. because of lightning and a door needing repair.</p><p>Perhaps facetiously, Gonzalez said he worried the extra two hours would give Sox brass time to reconsider bringing him to Rate Field.</p><p>“I was just hoping they weren’t going to change their minds,” Gonzalez said. “I was going to turn my phone off and stay on the flight.”</p><p>The Sox didn’t change their minds, but Gonzalez is c<a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/05/24/white-sox-prospects-jacob-gonzalez-braden-montgomery" >hanging how he is perceived</a>.</p><p>After struggling at multiple minor-league levels in both 2024 and 2025, Gonzalez has broken out this year at Triple-A Charlotte. In 52 games, Gonzalez has 19 home runs, a .419 on-base percentage and .668 slugging percentage.</p><p>“He's crushing baseballs is what he's been doing,” Sox manager <b>Will Venable </b>said. “It's really impressive.”</p><p>Travel issues aside, the lefthanded-hitting Gonzalez wasn’t slated to start Saturday against Tigers left-hander <b>Framber Valdez</b>. At least to begin, Gonzalez will play first base against righties to keep the rest of the infield intact.</p><p>“I’ll play anywhere,” said Gonzalez, who’s played six games at first in the minors. “I grew up playing everywhere and ready to help this team win some games.”</p><p>To make room for Gonzalez on the 40-man roster, the Sox moved <b>Jordan Leasure</b> (right flexor strain) to the 60-day injured list.</p><h2>Q-rating</h2><p>Catcher <b>Edgar Quero </b>also had an eventful day.</p><p>The Sox gave away bobbleheads featuring him and fellow catcher <b>Kyle Teel</b>. Minutes before the game, Quero’s wife <b>Maira</b> threw him a ceremonial first pitch. Then, despite a day of taking a beating behind the plate, Quero hit his second home run of the season, a solo homer in the seventh that gave the Sox a 3-1 lead.</p><p>With two hits, Quero raised his average to .196 and is showing signs of improvement at the plate.</p><p>“I was feeling pretty good [over] the last couple of games, making a couple adjustments in my setup in the box,” Quero said. “Feeling pretty good right now."</p><h2>Taylor-made</h2><p>When <b>Randal Grichuk </b>dropped a fly ball in right, the Tigers got runners to first and second with no outs in the sixth. Reliever <b>Grant Taylor </b>replaced starter <b>Anthony Kay</b>, and Detroit’s rally stopped there.</p><p>Taylor got through the inning scoreless, picking up a strikeout, a flyout and a grounder. Taylor was better in the seventh, striking out the side.</p><p>“He pretty much saved the day there,” said Kay, who went five innings and allowed a run. “First and second, no outs and [for] him to retire three guys was massive. The boys tacked on and kind of made it a comfortable win.”</p><h2><b>In brief</b></h2><p><b>Derek Hill </b>(upper back tightness) was a late scratch. He was replaced in center field by <b>Rikuu Nishida</b>.<br>* Outfielder <b>Jarred Kelenic </b>cleared waivers and declined an outright assignment, making him a free agent.</p>
